title: God's Wildest Object Lesson: A Prophet, a Prostitute, and Their Kids
paragraphs: So, here's the scoop from God, delivered to Hosea, son of Beeri. This all went down while Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were running things in Judah, and Jeroboam son of Joash was king in Israel.
§This Whole Country Has Become a Whorehouse
The very first thing God ever said to Hosea was, no cap, pretty wild.
He said, “Go find a prostitute and marry her. Start a family with her. And here’s the reason: this entire country has basically become a giant brothel, cheating on me, their God.”
And Hosea just... did it. He went and married Gomer, the daughter of Diblaim. She got pregnant and had a son.
Then God told him:

“Name that kid Jezreel. It won’t be long before I make the whole nation of Israel answer for the massacre that happened at Jezreel. I’m officially calling it quits on the kingdom of Israel. Payday is coming, and I’m going to smash all their weapons to bits in the Valley of Jezreel.”
Gomer got pregnant again, and this time it was a girl. God told Hosea:

“Name her No-Mercy. I am so over Israel. I’ve run out of mercy. There are no more second chances. Judah, though, that’s a different situation. I’ll keep having mercy on them. I’ll save them. And it’ll be me, their God, who does the saving—not their military, not their weapons, not their cavalry or their soldiers.”
After Gomer had weaned No-Mercy, she got pregnant yet again and had another son. God said:
“Name him Nobody. Because you all have become nobodies to me, and I, God, am a nobody to you.

“But hold up, plot twist. Down the road, the population of Israel is going to explode. You won't even be able to count them, like grains of sand on the beach. And in the exact spot where they were called ‘Nobody,’ they’ll be called ‘Children of the Living God.’ Everyone from Judah and Israel will get back together as one crew. They’ll pick a single leader and become an unstoppable force. That’s gonna be a goated day for Jezreel!”

title: From Toxic to Forever: God's Comeback Story
paragraphs: Rename your brothers 'God's Somebody.' Rename your sisters 'All Mercy.'
§Wild Weekends and Unholy Holidays

"Time to drag your mother into court and call her out. She's not my wife anymore, and I'm not her husband. Tell her to quit dressing like a whore, putting herself on display for sale. If she won't stop, I'll rip her clothes right off and leave her exposed, naked as the day she was born. I'll turn her skin into dried-out leather, her body into a desert wasteland, nothing but a rack of bones in the middle of nowhere. I want nothing to do with her kids either — every single one of them was born in a whorehouse. Face it: your mother has been a whore, bringing bastard children into this world. She said, 'I'm off to see my lovers! They'll wine and dine me, dress me up, perfume me, shower me with jewelry!' But I'll fix her — I'll dump her in a field of thistles and ditch her in a dead-end alley. She'll go hunting for her lovers but won't land a single one. She'll search high and low but come up empty. Then she'll say, 'I'm going back to my first husband, the one I started out with. That life was so much better than this.' What she never got was that it was me all along who wined and dined and dressed her up — me who put her in those big-city fashions and jewelry that she wasted at wild Baal-worship parties. I'm about to cut her off: no more wining and dining! Her silk and fancy dresses are history. I'll expose her in front of everyone, and all her fly-by-night lovers won't be able to do a thing to help her. Party time is over. I'm shutting down the whole operation — her wild weekends and unholy holidays. I'll wreck her fancy gardens and decorative fountains, the ones she bragged about: 'My whoring paid for all this!' They'll end up as garbage dumps, feeding grounds for stray dogs and cats. I'll make her pay for her whole promiscuous-religion thing — all that steamy Baal worship and all the cheating sex that came with it, stalking her lovers all dressed to kill, with not a single thought for me." That's God's Message.
§To Start All Over Again

But here's what I'm going to do — I'm hitting reset and starting all over. I'm taking her back out into the wilderness, to the place where we had our first date, and I'm going to court her all over again. I'll give her bouquets of roses. I'll turn Heartbreak Valley into Acres of Hope. She'll respond to me like she did when she was young, back in those fresh-out-of-Egypt days.

"On that day" — this is still God's Message — "you'll call me 'Dear husband!' Never again will you call me 'My slave-master!' I'll wash your mouth out with soap and get rid of every dirty false-god name — you won't even whisper them again. At the same time I'll make a peace treaty between you and the wild animals, the birds, and the reptiles, and get rid of every weapon of war. Think about it! Safe from beasts and bullies! And then I'll marry you for good — forever! I'll marry you true and proper, in love and tenderness. Yes, I'll marry you and never leave you or let you go. You'll know me, God, for who I really am."

"On that very day, I'll answer" — this is God's Message — "I'll answer the sky, the sky will answer the earth, the earth will answer the grain and the wine and the olive oil, and they'll all answer Jezreel. I'll plant her in the good earth. I'll have mercy on No-Mercy. I'll say to Nobody, 'You're my dear Somebody,' and he'll say, 'You're my God!'"

title: God Said Get My Cheating Wife Back?!
paragraphs: §In Time They'll Come Back

Then God was like, “Alright, do it all over again. Go get your wife back, even though she’s with her new guy. Yeah, your cheating wife. Love her the same way I, God, love the people of Israel, even when they’re out there chasing every other god they see.”

So I did it. I paid a good chunk of change to get her back—cost me about as much as a slave. Then I told her straight up, “From now on, you’re living with me. No more hooking up, no more sleeping around. You’re with me, and I’m with you. Period.”

This is a picture of what’s going to happen with the Israelites. They’re going to spend a long time feeling totally lost and alone, without a king or any leader, without any real religion or way to connect with God. It’s gonna be a rough time.

But, plot twist, they’ll come back. The Israelites will eventually start looking for their God and their true king, the one from David's line. They’ll come back humbled, totally in awe of God and all the amazing things He does. They'll be ready for the epic finale of His love story.

title: God Calls Out the Fakes
paragraphs: §No One Is Faithful

Yo, Israel, listen up! God's got a major bone to pick with everyone. He's like, 'Nobody's loyal. Nobody's got love. Nobody even gets me.' It's just non-stop cursing, lying, murder, stealing, and sleeping around. Total chaos, just one person getting iced after another. And because of all this, the whole country is basically crying. Everything's messed up—the animals, the birds, even the fish are just floating around, totally dead inside.

But don't even try to point fingers. You, the priests, you're the ones getting called out. You're tripping all day, and then the so-called prophets take over and trip all night. Your mother is as bad as you. God's people are getting wrecked 'cause they don't know what's real anymore. Since you priests ghosted on true knowledge, God's ghosting you. You ignored what God showed you, so now he's ignoring your kids. The more of you there are, the more sin there is. You traded your honor for cheap thrills. You get fat off of people's screw-ups and can't wait for them to do more messed-up stuff. Now, you can't even tell who's who—the priests are just as bad as everyone else. God's about to make everyone face the music for their trash lifestyle. They'll eat but still be starving, hook up but never feel satisfied. They totally bailed on their God to chase after cheap hookups.
§They Make a Picnic Out of Religion

My people are basically wasted on booze. They're out here asking dead trees for advice and expecting a stick to give them answers. They're so drunk on sex they can't even think straight. They've swapped out God for their own desires. They're having religious 'parties' up on mountains, just chilling under trees like it's a festival. Next thing you know, your own daughters are selling their bodies and your sons' wives are cheating. But God's not even coming after the girls. He's coming after the men who are paying for it, the guys who are worshipping at these gross sex-shrines. What a clueless generation, getting ruined by this stuff.

You really messed up your own life, Israel—but don't you dare drag Judah down with you! Don't go to the sex-shrine at Gilgal, and stay away from that sin-city Bethel. And don't go around saying 'God bless' when you don't even mean it, just throwing His name around. Israel is being stubborn, like a mule that won't move. How is God supposed to lead them into a good place like a gentle lamb? Ephraim is literally addicted to his idols. Just let him be. Once the party's over, it's all about sex, sex, and more sex. They love their shameless, dirty lifestyle. But a storm is coming to snatch them up, and their whole sex-worshipping thing will leave them empty and powerless.

title: God's Done Playing Games
paragraphs: §They Wouldn't Recognize God If They Saw Him

Alright, listen up, you priests! And pay attention, people of Israel! Royal family, you better be all ears too! You're supposed to be the ones in charge of justice, but what have you actually been doing? You've been taking advantage of people at Mizpah, scamming them on Tabor, and totally victimizing them at Shittim. So yeah, I'm about to bring the hammer down on all of you.

I see right through you, Ephraim. For real, Israel, I know exactly what you're up to. Ephraim, you've been messing around with your gross mix of sex and fake religion for way too long. The whole nation of Israel is just...toxic. You guys couldn't even turn back to God if you wanted to. Your whole lifestyle is a seriously bad habit. Every move you make is messed up. You wouldn't even recognize God if you saw him.

Your arrogance is off the charts, and honestly, it's a public embarrassment. All of you—Israel, Ephraim, and Judah—are just stumbling around in your own guilt. And when you finally decide to get your act together and look for God again, it's gonna be too late. I, God, will be long gone. You've been disloyal to me for way too long, and now your country is filling up with your illegitimate kids. A massive plague is about to wreck your trashed land.

Sound the alarms in Gibeah and Ramah! Signal the invasion of Sin City! Freak Benjamin out! Ephraim is going to be left completely destroyed, like a wasteland. I'm giving it to you straight, no sugar-coating, tribes of Israel.
Israel's leaders are just a bunch of crooks and thieves. They're cheating people out of their own land, and I am so, so angry. My anger is going to hit every single part of them.

Ephraim has been brutal, and now he's about to get brutalized himself—a taste of his own medicine. He was so obsessed with doing things his own useless way. Because of that, I'm going to be like an infection to Ephraim, and like a rot that destroys the house of Judah.

When Ephraim realized he was sick and Judah saw his nasty, infected sores, Ephraim ran off to Assyria for help from their 'great' king. But plot twist: he can't heal you. He can't fix the mess you're in.

I'm about to go full-on grizzly bear on Ephraim, and like a mama bear with cubs on Judah. I'll tear them to pieces, for real. No one can stop me. I'll drag them off, and no one will be able to rescue them. Then, I'll go back to my place and wait until they finally get a clue. When they finally hit rock bottom, maybe then they'll start looking for me.

title: God's Tough Love: Time for a Real Comeback
paragraphs: §Gangs of Priests Assaulting Worshipers

Alright, let's get real and go back to God. He might have let us get hurt, but He's the one who can heal us. He hit us hard, no cap, but He'll patch us up. Give it a couple of days, and we'll start feeling ourselves again. By day three, He'll have us rebooted—brand-new, alive, and ready to face Him. We're so ready to actually get to know God, like, for real. His return is as certain as the sunrise. He shows up like a much-needed rain shower, like that spring rain that makes everything fresh.

But for real, what am I supposed to do with you, Ephraim? And you, Judah, what's your deal? Your promises of love are about as long-lasting as the morning fog—here one second, gone the next. That's why I've been sending prophets to give you a major wake-up call, why my words are meant to cut deep: to make you see my judgment shining like a spotlight. I'm looking for a love that's legit, not just more religious rituals. I want you to actually *know* me, not just show up to more prayer meetings. You broke our deal, just like Adam did! You betrayed me, you ungrateful bunch.

Gilead is basically Crime City now—blood all over the sidewalks, all over the streets. It used to be that robbers would jump people. Now it's whole crews of priests attacking worshippers on their way to Shechem. They have zero respect for anything sacred.
I saw some seriously messed up stuff going down in Israel. Ephraim is out here worshipping at some shady religious spot, and Israel is right there with him, getting dragged through the mud.
And you're just as bad, Judah. You've been out here living wild. Well, guess what? It's harvest time.
changes: Ch6: added missing MSG § header 'Gangs of Priests Assaulting Worshipers'; text complete vs MSG

title: Israel's Self-Destruct Mode is ON
paragraphs: §Despite All the Signs, Israel Ignores God

Every time I tried to give Israel a fresh start, like wiping the slate clean to get them going again, Ephraim would just immediately mess it all up with new sins. The betrayal of Samaria was basically on full display. They're so two-faced and full of lies, they'll rob you blind and leave you with nothing. It's like it never even occurs to them that I'm keeping a running list of all their crimes. They're covered head to toe in the evidence of their sin. I see exactly who they are and what they've been up to.

They put on this whole evil circus for the king, and the princes are totally entertained by their acrobatic lies. They're just a bunch of thirsty cheaters, like an oven that stays hot from the moment the dough is kneaded until it rises.

On the king's holiday, the princes get wasted on wine, caught up in the craziness of the mocking crowd. They're like old-school wood stoves, glowing red-hot with lust. Their passion just simmers all night, then explodes into hungry flames in the morning. They're murderous and explosive, burning through their own rulers. Their kings keep falling, one after another, and not a single person even thinks to look my way.

Ephraim is mixing in with people who don't know God, just wasting his potential. Ephraim is like a pancake that's only cooked on one side—totally half-baked. Strangers are draining his strength, and he doesn't even have a clue. He's getting old and weak, and he doesn't notice that either.
His arrogance is a huge, public embarrassment. Israel just stumbles around, completely oblivious to God, ignoring all the warning signs and paying God no attention.

Ephraim is so clueless, a total airhead. First, he's chirping for Egypt to help, then he's fluttering over to Assyria. But I'm gonna throw my net over them and clip their wings. I'll teach them to listen to me! They're doomed! They've run away from me, and now they're in for some serious trouble. They've defied me, and I'm supposed to rescue them while they're feeding me a bunch of lies? Instead of genuinely praying to me, they're just partying in bed with prostitutes and doing these wild, self-harming rituals for their fake gods, all while turning their backs on me. I'm the one who gave them sharp minds and strong bodies, and how do they repay me? By plotting evil against me. They're always turning, but never toward me—they're like a broken weather vane, spinning all over the place. Their leaders will get taken down, murdered—which is exactly what they deserve for their disrespectful trash-talk. And the final verdict? They'll be a total laughingstock on the world stage.
changes: Ch7: added missing MSG § header 'Despite All the Signs, Israel Ignores God'

title: Israel's Epic Fail: Fake Gods & Big Problems
paragraphs: §Altars for Sinning

“Yo, blow the trumpet! Sound the alarm! Vultures are literally circling over God’s people because they completely broke my covenant and ignored my rules. And what’s their response? They cry out, ‘My God! We know you!’ but their actions are screaming the opposite. Israel wants nothing to do with what’s good, and now the enemy is hot on their trail.

They’re crowning kings without even asking me. They set up princes but totally left me out of the loop. Instead, they’re making idols from their silver and gold, and those very idols are gonna be their downfall. Just throw that gold calf-god on the trash heap, Samaria! I’m seething with anger against that piece of junk! How long until they finally get it together? And they’re supposed to be Israelites! A sculptor made that thing—it’s not God. That Samaritan calf is going to be smashed into a million pieces. Look at them! They’re planting wind-seeds, and they’re about to harvest a whole tornado. Their wheat has no head, so it makes no flour. And even if it did, strangers would just come and wolf it down. Israel is swallowed up and spit right back out. Among the other nations, they’re seen as a piece of junk. They ran off to Assyria—like, seriously? Even wild donkeys stick with their own kind, but Ephraim is out there paying for lovers. Now, because of their wild life among the pagans, I’m going to gather them all and confront them. They’re about to reap the consequences and feel what it’s like to be crushed by a powerful king.

Ephraim has built a ton of altars, and then he turns around and uses them for sinning. Can you even believe that? Altars for sinning! I write out my revelation for them in super clear detail, and they act like they can’t even read it. They offer sacrifices to me and then just feast on the meat themselves. God is not pleased. I’m so done—I’ll keep remembering their guilt. I’m going to punish their sins and send them straight back to Egypt. Israel has forgotten his Maker and gotten busy building palaces. Judah has gone all-in on building fortress cities. Well, I’m sending fire on their cities to burn down every single one of their fortifications.”
changes: Ch8: added missing MSG § header 'Altars for Sinning'; text complete vs MSG (incl. 'That Samaritan calf will be broken to bits', 'donkey-Ephraim goes out and pays to get lovers')

title: Party's Over, Israel. Payday's Here.
paragraphs: §Starved for God

Yo Israel, stop wasting your life on wild parties with people who don't follow God. You're constantly ditching your God, selling yourselves out at every sketchy sex-and-religion street festival like a cheap knockoff.

All that party food isn't going to satisfy you. You'll just end up feeling more empty. Seriously, you won't last in God's country at this rate. Some of you will end up broke in Egypt, others will get a harsh reality check in Assyria. As refugees, you won't get to worship God much—you'll be on basic rations, and your souls will get tainted by the spiritually toxic air. You'll be starving for a real connection with God, exiled from His land. Think you'll miss the holy days then? Bet you'll be homesick for the big festivals.

But watch out. When you think you've escaped one disaster, you'll land right in another one in Egypt. And Egypt will be the one throwing your funeral! What good will all your precious silver be then, when you're just trying to survive in a field full of weeds?

Time's up. Judgment is knocking. It's payday. Israel was all talk, saying, "The prophet's a psycho! This 'man of the Spirit' is insane!" But think again. Your massive guilt means you're in for some massive trouble. The prophet is watching out for Ephraim, doing God's work, but everyone's trying to trip him up. He's being hated in God's own house, of all places. People are just getting worse, almost as bad as that messed-up crime back in Gibeah. And God is keeping receipts. He's going to make them pay for every single sin.
§They Took to Sin Like a Pig to Filth

"A long time ago, when I first found Israel, it was like discovering grapes in the middle of a desert. Finding your ancestors was like finding the first figs of the season. But then they got to Baal-peor, that pagan spot, and they dove into sin like it was nothing, getting all buddy-buddy with their new idols. Ephraim's crew is so flaky, scattered like a bunch of birds, their potential just wasted in chaos. All noise, no substance, totally barren. Nothing to show for it—no new life, no babies.

And even if they managed to have kids, I'd have to say they're unfit parents and take them away. Seriously, it'll be a dark day for them when I just turn my back and walk away. I see Ephraim letting his kids run wild. He might as well be leading them straight to their own destruction!"
God, give them what they deserve! But what? Give them wombs that can't have kids and dried-up breasts.

"All their evil was exposed at that pagan shrine in Gilgal. Man, I hated them for that. Because of all their messed-up actions, I'm kicking them out of my land. I'm done wasting my love on them. Their leaders are just a bunch of rebellious teens. Ephraim is toast—roots dried up, no more fruit. And even if, by some miracle, they had kids, those precious babies wouldn't survive. I'd make sure of it!"
My God is so done with them. They just wouldn't listen. Now they're doomed to be wanderers, drifting aimlessly among nations that don't know God.

Ch9: re-badged to MSG ranges (1/2-5/6->1-6 x3, 10-11/12-13->10-13 x2); text complete vs MSG

title: Israel's Epic Fail: Fake Worship & Broken Promises
paragraphs: §You Thought You Could Do It All on Your Own

Israel was like a super productive vine, always loaded with grapes. But the more successful they got, the more they messed around with fake gods. The richer they became, the more cash they blew on idols they made up themselves. Their friendly smiles are totally fake. They're 100% guilty. God's about to smash their little worship spots and grind their statues into dust.

Then they'll be like, “A king? Who needs one? We don't even care about God, so why would a king matter? What could he even do for us?” They talk a big game, tell a bunch of lies, and make empty promises. But all their talk is just trash blowing in the wind.

The folks in Samaria are heading over to 'Crime City' to worship a golden calf idol. They're making a huge scene, dancing and shouting, totally fooled by their show-off priests. They act all important around this calf statue, but they have no idea it's all a scam and a total embarrassment. They're even planning to ship it to Assyria as a gift for the big king. That's how Ephraim is making a clown of himself, and Israel is getting shamed by its dumb idols.

Samaria is done for. Its king is like a dead branch floating down the river. And all of Israel's favorite places to sin will be destroyed. Thistles and crabgrass will be the only things decorating their busted altars. Then they'll be screaming at the mountains, “Bury us!” and begging the hills, “Fall on us!”

You guys have been sinning since day one at Gibeah—that crazy, messed-up, ancient sin—and you just never stopped. So, a war is coming to Gibeah to put an end to all this sinning. I'm going to show up and teach them a lesson. Nations will team up against them and make them learn the hard way the sum of Gibeah plus Gibeah.

Ephraim was like a trained calf that loved the easy work of threshing. I saw how strong and sleek she was and wanted to put a harness on her, get her working in the fields—with Judah plowing and Jacob breaking up the ground. I told you: 'Plant righteousness, and you'll harvest love. It's time to get the ground ready, time to seek God until he shows up with a harvest of justice.' But instead, you plowed wickedness, harvested evil, and ate a salad of lies. You thought you could handle everything on your own because you had so many weapons and soldiers. But a war is about to explode on your people. All your forts will be destroyed, just as brutally as when King Shalman destroyed the town of Beth-arbel, smashing mothers and their kids on the rocks. That's what's coming for you, you so-called people of God, because your evil is completely off the charts. One morning, you're gonna wake up and find that Israel, its king, and its kingdom are just... gone. Nothing left.

title: God's Uncancelable Love
paragraphs: §Israel Played at Religion with Toy Gods

“When Israel was just a kid, I loved him so much. I called him out of Egypt, like, ‘That’s my son!’ But the more other people called his name, the more he ran away from me. He started worshipping all the popular fake gods and messing around with idols.

Still, I was the one who stuck by him. I taught Ephraim how to walk, I rescued him from getting stuck. But he never even gave me a shout-out, never admitted I was the one giving him a ride, lifting him up like a baby to my cheek, and bending down to feed him. Now he wants to go back to Egypt or run off to Assyria—literally anywhere but back to me! That’s why his cities are a total mess, the murder rate is insane, and every plan they make just falls apart. My people are just hell-bent on leaving me. They’re praying to this Baal guy for help, but he’s not lifting a finger for them.

But for real, how can I just give up on you, Ephraim? How can I let you go, Israel? How could I ever let you get wrecked like Admah or destroyed like Zeboim? I can’t even stand the thought of it. My stomach is churning just thinking about it. So, I’m not gonna act on my anger. I’m not gonna destroy Ephraim. You know why? Because I’m God, not some human. I’m the Holy One, and I’m right here with you.

“In the end, the people will follow God. I’ll roar like a lion—a massive roar! And my kids will come running back from the west, all scared and shaky. They’ll fly back from Egypt like frightened birds, and from Assyria like scared doves. And I’ll bring them all right back to their homes.” That’s God’s Word!
§Soul-Destroying Lies
“Ephraim is all about lies, 24/7. You can’t trust a single thing Israel says. And Judah? No better. They’re addicted to cheap, fake gods.”

title: Don't Get Scammed by Fake Gods
paragraphs: Ephraim is all about chasing fantasies, like they're trying to catch ghosts or something. They're constantly telling lies, the kind that really mess with your soul. Both Ephraim and Judah tried to make deals with Assyria and get on Egypt's good side.

God's basically taking Israel to court. Jacob's descendants are getting called out and punished for their actions. Back in the womb, Jacob, that little heel, totally got one over on his brother. And when he grew up, he tried to pull the same thing on God. But you can't outplay God. God put him in his place. Jacob ended up on his knees, crying and praying. God met him at Bethel, and that's where they had a real talk. God is the God of Angel Armies, the God who reveals Himself, the God we can know.
So what are you even waiting for? Go back to your God! Be all about love and justice. Wait for your God, and don't ever give up on him!

The business guys are running a total scam. They love ripping people off! Ephraim was bragging, “Yo, I'm rich! I made it! And I'm so good at covering my tracks, you can't find a single trace of scamming or sin!”

“But hold up,” says God, “I'm your God, the one who was with you back in Egypt! I'm gonna make you live in tents again, just like the old days when you used to worship in the desert. I speak through the prophets to show you what's really going on. I use them to tell stories that reveal the truth. I'm showing how Gilead is a hotbed of religious drama and Gilgal is full of empty-headed religion. Their so-called worship spots are just like stinking piles of trash in their own backyards.”

Are you seriously going to be like your ancestor Jacob? He ran away to Aram all guilty, then basically sold his soul to get rich, making it big through lies and scams. Your true identity comes from the prophets God sent, the ones who led you out of Egypt and were like faithful pastors to you. But Ephraim has just kept on disrespecting God, no excuses. Now he's gotta pay the price for his destructive lifestyle. His Master is going to give him a taste of his own medicine.

title: God's Done Playing Games
paragraphs: §Religion Customized to Taste

Back in the day, God basically told Ephraim (part of Israel) that they were on thin ice. They got caught up in some seriously messed-up worship of a fake god, Baal, and it spiritually wrecked them. And guess what? They're doing it again, creating their own designer gods, whatever they feel like. They've got people who will literally make you any god you want. It's wild. They're sacrificing babies to these dead statues and kissing golden calves. Can you believe it? And now there's nothing left of these people — hollow men, desiccated women, like scraps of paper blown down the street, like smoke in a gusty wind.

God's like, "Yo, I'm still your God, the one who got you out of Egypt. I'm the only real God you've ever known, the only one who actually saves you. I took care of you when you were struggling in the desert with nothing. I gave you everything you needed, and you got spoiled. You got arrogant and thought you didn't need me. You straight-up forgot me.

So now I'm coming for you like a lion, like a leopard hiding in the grass. I'm going to be like a mama bear whose cubs were stolen — I'll rip out their guts. Coyotes will make a meal of them. Crows will clean their bones. I'm gonna destroy you, Israel, and who's gonna stop me? Where's that king you thought would save you? Where are all those leaders you begged for? All these rulers you insisted on having, demanding, 'Give me a king! Give me leaders!'? Well, I gave you one, even though I wasn't happy about it, and now I'm done with him. I've been keeping receipts of all your cheating—all of Ephraim's sin is on record.

When it was time for Ephraim to be 'born' into something new, they were too dumb to even come out. The way to life was wide open, and they just stood there. Should I save them? Should I rescue them from death? Nah. Who's scared of you, Death? Your threats are nothing. In the end I'm done with regret, done with sorrow — even though Ephraim ran wild, the black sheep of the family.

A tornado from God is heading straight for them from the desert. It's going to completely wreck the country, leaving nothing but ruins. The cities will be trashed, and all their precious stuff will be gone. Now Samaria has to pay up for rebelling against their God. Their people will be killed, their babies smashed against rocks, and their pregnant women attacked."

title: The Ultimate Comeback Story
paragraphs: §Come Back! Return to Your God!

Yo, Israel, come on back to your God! Seriously, you've messed up, but it's not over. Get your apology ready and come back to God. Just pray something like, 'God, please forgive all our screw-ups. We're coming clean. Our promises to change are the real deal. Assyria's not gonna save us, and all those fancy horses? They're not getting us anywhere. We're done calling our own creations 'god.' You're literally our only hope. It's true that you're the one who shows mercy to the helpless, right?'

God's like, 'I'm going to fix their rebellious streak. I'm gonna love them like crazy. I'm not mad anymore. It's a clean slate for Israel. They're gonna blossom like a flower in spring and put down roots as strong as an oak tree. They'll stand tall like a cedar tree, and smell as sweet as a cedar grove. The people living near them will be blessed because of them, and they'll thrive like a field of golden wheat. Everyone will be talking about them, saying they're the OG children of God. Ephraim is so over those fake gods. From now on, I'm the one who's got his back. I'm like a tree that's always loaded with fruit. Everything you could ever need, you can find in me.'

If you want to live a good life, you gotta understand this. If you know what's good for you, you'll learn this stuff by heart. God's ways are the right ways to go. People who live right can walk them no problem, but people who do wrong are always tripping over themselves.
